rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a ZrN interlayer between Cr and Zr-alloy, while the target paper uses a compositionally varied AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy coating without an interlayer. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions ~300°C normal operation and ~900°C steam transients, whereas the target paper tests isothermal oxidation at 1000°C and 1100°C in flowing steam. The temperature regimes and exposure specifics differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on a ZrN diffusion barrier to suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion. The target paper's mechanism involves formation of a protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite oxide layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion, with excess Al causing detrimental intermetallics. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interdiffusion and better protection than a Cr-only baseline. The target paper predicts and finds an optimum Al content (~10 at.%) minimizing oxidation and oxygen penetration, with excessive Al reversing the benefit. The predicted property (oxidation resistance vs. interdiffusion) and the nature of the comparison differ.
